$comment: PRD section 6 price model. Price = base * (reference / max(stock, 1)) ^ elasticity, clamped, with a buy/sell spread by settlement type. The reference is the same demand level for every town of a size; what differs is the stock each town drifts back to: producers hold more (cheap), consumers less (dear). That gap is what makes trade routes pay. Ports live (towns): each has people (by size, more at a capital) whose fields and workshops make goods and whose households eat them every day, as a port's profile says; chains turn one good into another unit for unit (rum from sugar, cloth from cotton) only from what is in store. The wider world (the hinterland, smugglers, ships from Europe) closes 'pull' of the gap to the usual stock each day, so a port that makes or eats 'netShare' x pull x its usual stock a day sits half that again above or below it when no merchant calls. People grow 'up' a week while their needs are 'satisfied' (stock against usual) and fall 'down' a week when 'starved', within min..max of their size's people. The merchant's purse is perPerson gold a head, refilling 'refill' of the gap a day: he buys only what it covers. Coasting craft between ports within 'tiles' at peace move 'share' of their stock gap (up to 'max' units a good a day).

shocks.$comment: Market shocks (PRD section 6): each moves one good at one town. 'on' picks a good the town exports or wants (a notable lean). 'stock' multiplies its usual stock while the shock lasts, and the market jumps 'jolt' of the way there at once so it shows on the next visit. About 'perWeek' shocks start each week across the map; storms add 'storm' shocks to every export of a town their eye passes over. Shocks last at least 4 weeks so news of one can still be acted on after crossing the map.

bumper.news: A bumper {good} harvest at {town}: {good} is going cheap there.

blight.news: Blight has struck the {good} at {town}. It is scarce and dear.

shortage.news: {town} has run short of {good}; merchants there pay handsomely.

famine.news: Famine at {town}: the harvest has failed and food is dear. The governor pays for every load landed.

storm.news: A storm has wrecked the {good} at {town}. It will be dear there for weeks.

news.$comment: News spreads from its town at 'tilesPerDay' (a little slower than a brig), plus a seeded delay. Items are kept 'keepWeeks' from when they happened; 10 weeks x 7 days x 80 tiles is well beyond the map's 1,950-tile diagonal, so every town hears before an item is dropped.

contracts.$comment: Tavern contracts (PRD section 6): every shortage and famine is also the governor's offer for the goods it lacks, heard wherever its news has reached. 'units' is 'share' of the town's reference stock of the good, rounded to 5, within 'units'; the reward, paid when all are landed (sold to the town's merchant, on top of the sale), is units x the good's base price x 'perUnit', at least 'minPerUnit' a unit (so food, too cheap to carry for profit, pays). It lasts as long as the shortage; filling it ends the shortage.

plague.$comment: Plague (PRD section 6, events): about 'perWeek' outbreaks a week across the map, at towns of 'minPeople' or more; it lasts 'weeks', shuts the port to all shipping (the player, merchants, coasting craft) and its people fall 'down' a week on top of any hunger. A ship that sailed from a plagued port brings it to her next port at 'spread' odds.
plague.news: Plague has broken out at {town}. The port is shut to shipping.
